title: Myrtle Beach Condo Financing: 2026 Loan Rules Explained
description: Buying a condo in Myrtle Beach? What the 2026 condo rules changed, condo-hotels and rental programs, renting your unit, and loans if a building fails.
h1: Myrtle Beach Condo Financing: What the 2026 Rules Mean for Buyers
dek: Oceanfront tower, resort building or a small complex off the beach? Here's how condo loans work on the Grand Strand now.

faq.q: Can you finance a condo-hotel in Myrtle Beach?
faq.a: Not with a regular Fannie Mae loan, because Fannie Mae won't back a loan in a building that runs like a hotel. You can still finance one with a non-warrantable condo loan from a lender that lends outside Fannie Mae's rules.

A non-warrantable condo is a unit in a building that doesn't meet Fannie Mae's rules, so it can't get a regular conventional loan sold to Fannie Mae. Common reasons are hotel-style operations, big unfunded repairs, one owner with too many units, or too much commercial space.

faq.q: Did Fannie Mae get rid of Limited Review for condos?
faq.a: Yes. Fannie Mae retired Limited Review for loan applications dated on or after August 3, 2026. Established buildings with more than 10 units now need a full review, FHA approval or a Fannie Mae review.

faq.q: Can I rent out my Myrtle Beach condo and still get a regular mortgage?
faq.a: Yes, if the building qualifies. Renting your own unit is fine. In the City of Myrtle Beach, short-term stays collect about 13% in lodging taxes, so build that into your plans.
